Rashi on Arakhin 5a:11:1.hebrew: דמי ראשי למזבח מי נידון בכבודו או אין נידון בכבודו - ויהיב פלגא דמים. והרי אין לך בעל מום למזבח גדול מזה — שהוא אדם — וקא מיבעיא ליה. ואמאי? תיפשוט ליה מההיא דאין נידון:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:11:1.english: “[The] value of my head to the altar” — is it assessed according to its significance, or is it not assessed according to its significance - And [so] he gives half the value. And behold, you have no greater blemished [entity] for the altar than this — for he is a human being — and [yet] this was a dilemma for him. And why? Let him resolve it from that [baraita], that it is not assessed [according to its significance].

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:12:1.hebrew: מי אמרי' לא אשכחן - נדר בשום דוכתא דאין נידון בכבודו, א"ד לא אשכחן לגבי מזבח כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:12:1.english: Do we say, "We have not found" - [Meaning,] a vow anywhere that is not assessed according to its dignity; or perhaps, we have not found regarding the altar, etc.?

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:13:1.english: [Is he] assessed according to affordability - In [the case of] a vow or freewill offering such as this?

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:15:1.english: [If] one consecrated an ancestral field - For the value of a burnt offering.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:15:2.hebrew: מהו - היכי פריק ליה אי בעי למיפרקיה? דהא פשיטא לן: אי אקדשיה לבדק הבית, הוה פריק בית זרע חומר שעורים בחמשים שקל כסף, דגזירת הכתוב הוא, ואפילו היא שוה אלף זוז:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:15:2.english: What is [the law] - How does he redeem it if he wishes to redeem it? For it is obvious to us: if he consecrated it for Temple maintenance, he would redeem an area requiring a ḥomer of barley seed for fifty silver shekels, as it is a scriptural decree, even if it is worth a thousand zuz.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:15:3.hebrew: שדה אחוזה דמיפרקא - דהא לא אשכחן שדה אחוזה אלא לבדק הבית, דסתם הקדישות לבדק הבית. הלכך, כי פריש לה למזבח, לא פריק לה נמי אלא בהכי? או דלמא, לא אשכחן למזבח אלא בשויו, דהא לא אשכחן קראי למזבח אלא בבהמות, והנהו ודאי לא נתנה תורה קצבה לפדיונן אם הוממו, והכא נמי אמרינן בשויו? תיקו:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:15:3.english: An ancestral field that is redeemed - For we have not found an ancestral field [consecrated] except for Temple maintenance, since unspecified consecrations are for Temple maintenance. Therefore, when he specified it for the altar, is it also redeemed only in this manner? Or perhaps, we have not found [anything consecrated] for the altar [redeemed] except according to its value, for we have not found verses [concerning consecrations] for the altar except regarding animals, and for those, the Torah certainly did not set a fixed rate for their redemption if they developed a blemish; and here too, do we say [that it is redeemed] according to its value? [The dilemma] stands unresolved.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:16:1.hebrew: פחות מבן חדש נידר - אם אמר אחר: "דמיו עלי", שהרי דמים כל דהו יש לו:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:16:1.english: [A child] less than a month old is vowed - If another [person] said, "His value is upon me," for he has some value.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:16:2.english: But is not valuated - For it is stated in the passage only from one month old and upward.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:17:1.english: He gives his value - How much he is sold for in the market.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:19:1.hebrew: כר"מ - דאמר: אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה, ואדם יודע דאין ערך לכלי — דנפשות כתיב — וגמר ואמר לשם דמים:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:19:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Meir - For he said: A person does not utter his words in vain, and a person knows that there is no valuation for a utensil — as “souls” [persons] is written [in the verse] — and [therefore] he resolved and spoke for the sake of [its monetary] value.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:19:2.english: [It is] obvious that [it is] in accordance with Rabbi Meir - Why did [the Gemara] need to say: "In accordance with whom does this follow?"

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:20:1.hebrew: התם - גבי פחות מבן חדש פטרי רבנן, משום דאיכא למימר: אפילו אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה, הני מילי היכא דהוא יודע שדבריו בטילין, אבל זה סבור היה שיש ערך לפחות מבן חדש כבן חדש, והרי אין לו, ונמצא הקדש טעות, ודמים לא קאמר דליתיב דמי; אבל גבי כלי ליחייב — קמ"ל דר"מ היא ולא רבנן, דטעמייהו דרבנן משום דאדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה, ואפילו הוא יודע שדבריו זה בטילין:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:20:1.english: There - In the case of [an infant] less than a month old, the Rabbis exempt [him] because it can be said: Even [if] a person does not issue his words for naught, this applies only where he knows that his words are void; but this [person] thought that there is a valuation for [an infant] less than a month old just as for [an infant] a month old, and behold, there is none for him, so it turns out to be a consecration in error, and he did not say "[market] value" that he should give [its] value; but in the case of a utensil, let him be obligated! — [Therefore,] it teaches us that it is [according to] Rabbi Meir and not the Rabbis, for the reasoning of the Rabbis is that a person does issue his words for naught, even when he knows that these words of his are void.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:2:1.english: It shall be sold for the needs of a burnt offering, and its proceeds are non-sacred - For he did not consecrate its body.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:2:2.hebrew: חוץ מדמי אבר - שלא יקבל דמה. כיון דנחתא ליה קדושת הגוף, אינו רשאי למוכרה, ואם מכרה — אינה מכורה, שהרי עולתו היא; וכיון דלא נפקא לחולין, דתמימה היא, אין קדושה חלה על מעות האבר, הלכך אינה מכורה. וא"ת: נמצא לוקח זה מקריב עולה חסירה אבר, שאין אבר זה שלו? הא פרכי' לה בפ"ק דתמורה (דף יא:), ומשנינן לה: כגון דאמר הרי עלי עולה בחייה:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:2:2.english: Except for the payment for the limb - That he should not receive its payment: Since bodily sanctity descended upon it, he is not permitted to sell it; and if he sold it, it is not sold, for it is his burnt offering. And since it does not go out to non-sacred status, as it is unblemished, sanctity does not take effect upon the money of the limb; therefore, it is not sold. And if you say: [If so,] this purchaser turns out to be sacrificing a burnt offering lacking a limb, as this limb is not his? Behold, we asked this in the first chapter of Temurah (folio 11b), and we resolved it: Such as where he said: "Behold, incumbent upon me is a burnt offering during its lifetime."

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:4:1.hebrew: ואפילו למ"ד כו' - הכי אוקימנא בשילהי פ"ק דתמורה (דף יא:), דלא פליגי ר"מ ורבי יהודה אלא בדבר שאין הנשמה תלויה בו, כגון מן הארכובה ולמטה:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:4:1.english: And even according to the one who says, etc. - So we established at the end of the first chapter of Temurah (11b), that Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree only regarding an item upon which life does not depend, such as from the knee downward.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג לא קשיא, ולא גרסי' אלא:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:5:1.english: This is the correct reading: "It is not difficult," and we do not read "Rather".

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:5:2.hebrew: הא בקדושת הגוף - הא דקתני פשטה קדושה בכולה, כגון דאקדשה קדושת הגוף, דאמר: ראש בהמה זו אקריב עולה. וברייתא דלעיל, דאין לקדשי מזבח אלא ראשה של פרה, כגון דאקדשה לדמים, דאמר: ראש בהמה זו עלי לדמי עולה — דומיא דעבד וחמור, דלא שייכא בהו קדושת הגוף להקרבה:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:5:2.english: This [refers to] inherent sanctity - That which is taught, that sanctity spreads throughout all of it, is [in a case] where he consecrated it with inherent sanctity, in that he said: "I will sacrifice the head of this animal as a burnt offering." And the baraita above, [which taught] that the altar's consecrated property has only the head of the cow, is [in a case] where he consecrated it for its value, in that he said: "The head of this animal is upon me for the value of a burnt offering" — similar to a slave and a donkey, to which inherent sanctity for sacrifice does not apply.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:6:1.hebrew: והא מר הוא דאמר - בפ"ק דתמורה (דף יא:): הקדיש זכר — איל דחזי לעולה — ואקדשיה לדמי עולה, קדוש קדושת הגוף, והוא עצמו יקרב עולה; דמיגו דנחתא ליה קדושת דמים, נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף, הואיל והוא חזי לגופיה. ה"נ, כי אמר: "ראש פרה לדמי עולה", תיקדש לגופה, (הוא) הואיל והיא חזיא, תפשוט קדושה בכולה:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:6:1.english: But wasn't it the Master who said - In the first chapter of Temurah (11b): [If] one consecrated a male [animal] — a ram that is fit for a burnt offering — and consecrated it for the value of a burnt offering, it is sanctified with inherent sanctity, and it itself shall be sacrificed as a burnt offering; for since sanctity of value descended upon it, inherent sanctity descended upon it, since it is fit in itself [to be sacrificed]. So too here, when one said: "The head of a cow is for the value of a burnt offering," let it be sanctified with inherent sanctity; (it) since it is fit [to be an offering], let the sanctity spread throughout all of it.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:7:1.hebrew: הא דאקדיש כוליה - לדמיו, קדוש קדושת הגוף, דליכא אלא חד מיגו:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:7:1.english: This is where he consecrated all of it - [When consecrated] for its value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity, for there is only one miggo.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:7:2.hebrew: הא דאקדיש חד אבר - כגון הכא, דאמר ראש פרה לדמי עולה, לא אמרינן: מיגו דקדיש חד אבר קדשה נמי כולה, ומיגו דנחתא ליה קדושת דמים נחתא ליה קדושת הגוף — דתרי מיגו לא אמרינן יחד:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:7:2.english: That [case is where] he consecrated one limb - For example, here, where he said, "The head of a cow is for the value of a burnt offering," we do not say: Since [migo] one limb is consecrated, the whole of it is also consecrated; and since [migo] monetary sanctity descended upon it, bodily sanctity descended upon it — for we do not say two migo [arguments] together.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:8:1.english: A limb as well was raised as a dilemma by the Master - At the end of the first chapter of Temurah (11b).

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:8:2.hebrew: הקדיש אבר לדמיו מהו - שתקדש כל הבהמה לגופה: מי אמרי': מיגו דקדיש חד אבר לדמי קדיש לגופיה, ומיגו דקדיש חד אבר קדשה כולה, א"ד תרי מיגו לא אמרינן? ואם איתא, תפשוט ליה למר מהא ברייתא דלא, דהא קתני: "אין להקדש אלא ראשה", ואוקמה לה בקדשי מזבח ודקאמר לדמי:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:8:2.english: [If] one consecrated a limb for its value, what is [the law] - [Is the question whether] the entire animal becomes sanctified with inherent sanctity? Do we say: Since [migo] one limb is consecrated for its value, it is consecrated with inherent sanctity; and since [migo] one limb is consecrated, the whole of it is consecrated — or perhaps we do not say two migo [arguments]? And if it is so, let it be resolved for the Master from this baraita that [it does] not [become sanctified], for behold, it teaches: "The consecrated property has only its head," and you established it as referring to items consecrated for the altar and where he said [it is] for its value.

Rashi on Arakhin 5a:9:1.hebrew: בתם - דאיכא למימר דתיחות ליה קדושת הגוף, דהא חזי להקרבה. וברייתא דפשיטא ליה דלא קדשה כולה — בבעל מום קא מיירי, דומיא דעבד וחמור, דלא חזו לגופייהו:
Rashi on Arakhin 5a:9:1.english: In [the case of] an unblemished [animal] - For it can be said that inherent sanctity should take effect upon it, since it is fit for sacrifice. And the baraita, where it is obvious that its entirety is not consecrated, is dealing with a blemished [animal], similar to a slave and a donkey, which are not fit [for sacrifice] in their own right.

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:10:1.hebrew: דבעי רבה דמי ראשי לגבי מזבח כו' תיקו - היינו מקמי דלשמעינן מתני' דלעיל, כדמסקינן:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:10:1.english: "As Rabba raised a dilemma: 'The value of my head to the altar, etc.' — teiku" - This was before we heard the Mishnah above, as we conclude.

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:11:1.hebrew: (בעי רבה דמי ראשי למזבח -) צריך עיון: אמאי לא נקט "ערך ראשי לגבי מזבח", כמו בבעיא דבסמוך:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:11:1.english: ("Rabba raised a dilemma: 'The value of my head to the altar'") - It requires further study: Why did he not state "the valuation of my head to the altar", as in the adjacent dilemma?

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:13:1.hebrew: בעי רבא ערכי עלי לגבי מזבח - אי רבה גרסי' בכולן, יש לפרש באם תמצא לומר, כדלעיל:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:13:1.english: Rava raised a dilemma: "My valuation is upon me for the altar" - If we read "Rabba" in all of them, it can be explained [as a progression of] "if you say" [im timtzeh lomar], as above.

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:21:1.hebrew: אדם יודע שאין ערך לפחות מבן חדש - ואפילו אינו יודע, מ"מ דעתו ע"פ שתקנו חכמים הלשון. וא"ת: מאי שנא מדאמר פרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סג.): "המתכוין לומר תרומה ואמר מעשר, מעשר ואמר תרומה — לא אמר כלום"? ויש לומר: דלא אמר כלום ממה שמוציא בפיו, אבל מה שבלבו הוי קיים. ועוד יש לומר: דהתם שאני, שמה שאמר בפיו אינו רוצה, ובמה שאמר בלבו טעה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:21:1.english: "A person knows that there is no valuation for [a child] less than one month old" - And even if he does not know, nevertheless his intent is in accordance with how the Sages established the language. And if you say: How is this different from what [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Tamid Nishchat (Pesachim 63a): "One who intended to say terumah and said ma'aser, [or intended to say] ma'aser and said terumah — he has said nothing"? And one can say that "he has said nothing" [applies only] to that which he uttered with his mouth, but that which was in his heart remains valid. And furthermore one can say that there it is different, for that which he uttered with his mouth he does not want, and regarding that which he said in his heart [i.e., intended], he erred.

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:2:1.hebrew: ימכר לצרכי עולה - וא"ת: וכי לוקח זה מקריב עולה חסירה אבר, שאין אבר זה שלו? הא פרכינן פ"ק דתמורה (דף יא:), ומשני: כגון דאמר "הרי עלי עולה בחייה", כלומר: כמו שיכול לחיות, ואע"פ שנחתך רגלה מן הארכובה ולמטה. והא דלא קא משני: כגון דאמר "רגלה של זו עולה לפטור עולתו של פלוני", כמ"ד פ"ק דחולין (דף כג:): "הרי עלי לחם לפטור תודתו של פלוני" — י"ל: דלא נקט לה אלא על לשון מימרא דאמורא, אבל לשון הברייתא לא מישתמע הכי:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:2:1.english: "It shall be sold for the needs of a burnt offering" - And if you say: Does this purchaser sacrifice a burnt offering lacking a limb, since this limb is not his? Behold, we raised this objection in the first chapter of Temurah (11b), and [the Gemara] answered: For example, where he said, "Behold, upon me is a burnt offering in its lifetime"—that is to say, as [long as] it is able to live, even though its leg was severed from the knee downward. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] did not answer: "For example, where he said: The leg of this [animal] is a burnt offering to exempt the burnt offering of so-and-so," like the one who said in the first chapter of Chullin (23b): "Behold, upon me is bread to exempt the thanks offering of so-and-so"? It can be answered: [The Gemara] adopts this only regarding the phrasing of an amoraic statement, but the phrasing of the Baraita does not imply this.

Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:6:1.hebrew: והא מר הוא דאמר הקדיש זכר לדמיו - מכאן משמע דגרסי' רבה, שלא אמר אביי "מר" לרבא חבירו. אע"ג דאשכחנא דאמר רב יוסף לאביי תלמידו: "מר דגברא רבה הוא ידע מאי קאמינא" בזבחים פ' קדשי קדשים (זבחים דף סב.) — התם שאני, שהבין אביי מה שלא הבינו אחרים:
Tosafot on Arakhin 5a:6:1.english: "But wasn't it the Master who said: [If one] consecrated a male for its value" - From here it is implied that we read 'Rabbah,' for Abaye would not say 'Master' to Rava, his colleague. Even though we find that Rav Yosef said to Abaye, his student: "The Master, who is a great man, knows what I am saying," in Zevachim, chapter Kodshei Kodashim (Zevachim 62a) — there it is different, because Abaye understood what others did not understand.
